title: Go Slices vs Arrays: Key Differences

scenes.say: Arrays and slices look similar in Go, but their behavior is very different. What makes slices special?

scenes.label: Fixed
scenes.sub: Arrays have a fixed length and can't grow.
scenes.say: Arrays in Go are fixed in size. Once you set their length, it never changes.

scenes.label: Dynamic
scenes.sub: Slices can grow and shrink. They track length and capacity.
scenes.say: Slices are dynamic. They track both length and capacity, and can change size as you append elements.
Arrays always keep their own storage. Slices are views over arrays, and appending can create a new backing array.
Here's the classic trap. After appending to s, it gets its own backing array. Changes to s won't affect a.

scenes.question: Does append always change the array?
scenes.right: No. Append only reallocates if capacity is exceeded. Otherwise, slices still share the same backing array.
scenes.say: Interviewers love this: append only reallocates if you exceed the slice's capacity. Otherwise, slices still share the same backing array.
